task: Task 17A.3 RESET P0 Production Rig Visual Direction Study
researchPolicy: Official publisher documentation and internal project specifications only.

sources.referenceTopic: Armature viewport display and Octahedral bones
sources.usefulPrinciple: Root, tip, envelope size and roll should remain legible in a compact diagnostic bone.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Use a square-section octahedral body with explicit root and tip endpoints in Candidate A.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not copy Blender mesh data, icons, UI chrome, or viewport styling.

sources.usefulPrinciple: Animator controls benefit from shapes distinct from deform bones.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Use a separate magenta control vocabulary in Candidate C.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not reproduce Blender widgets or theme assets.

sources.usefulPrinciple: A light structural rig can describe intent before a generated production rig exists.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Keep Candidate C as a static direction study rather than a generated functional rig.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not reproduce Rigify algorithms, source code, naming, or assets.

sources.referenceTopic: Controls, bones and nulls in Control Rig
sources.usefulPrinciple: Controls and hierarchy elements need visually distinct responsibilities.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Separate core bones, selection controls and aim/pole indicators in Candidate C.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not copy Control Rig node logic, gizmos, UI, or code.

sources.referenceTopic: Modular Control Rig connectors and sockets
sources.usefulPrinciple: Modular intent becomes clearer when connection regions are explicit.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Express pelvis, chest, hands and feet as readable regions without adding functional connectors.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not copy modules, connector implementations, samples, or assets.

sources.referenceTopic: Full Body IK controls and effectors
sources.usefulPrinciple: Effectors and pole intent should remain visually separate from skeletal links.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Use static hand/foot control outlines and elbow/knee pole diamonds only in Candidate C.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not implement FBIK, solvers, constraints, effectors, or Epic code.

sources.referenceTopic: Humanoid Avatar configuration and bone mapping
sources.usefulPrinciple: A humanoid overview benefits from an immediately recognizable body map and unambiguous required regions.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Keep the same 20-joint map in all three candidates and make Candidate B recognizably human.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not copy Unity avatar UI, silhouettes, bone mapping logic, or assets.

sources.usefulPrinciple: Interoperability starts from stable humanoid roles rather than display-specific geometry.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Preserve project joint IDs and parent relationships across every candidate.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not import VRM models, schemas, source code, or sample assets.

sources.usefulPrinciple: Hand semantics distinguish wrist/palm and directional digit chains.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Candidate B uses a palm plate and parallel digit hints without claiming a full tracked-hand skeleton.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Do not reproduce OpenXR runtime code, conformance data, or external hand assets.

sources.usefulPrinciple: Shared rig data, fixed hierarchy, segment lengths and one pose authority prevent divergent windows.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Freeze a Reference T snapshot sourced from HumanRigCore while keeping the prototypes fully disconnected from finalPose.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Reject any runtime binding, bone scaling, alternate hierarchy, or modification of HumanRigCore.

sources.referenceTopic: Character project and world-human system direction
sources.usefulPrinciple: One shared humanoid foundation should support character authoring, animation and multiple humans without visual drift.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Compare observation-first, crowd-first and editor-first display directions against the same body input.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Reject a new runtime page, NPC system, motion stack, mode switcher or behavior implementation.

sources.usefulPrinciple: Core, production and performance concerns should remain explicit layers.
sources.adoptedPrinciple: Limit P0 to display geometry and record its future suitability without implementing a performance layer.
sources.rejectedPrinciple: Reject performance deform, skin weights, anchors, limits, controllers and motion logic.
